title: Letter shapes: clue pairs one stroke apart in three fixed shape codings (16-segment, 5x7 dots, stroke list), against random and alphabet-distance-matched pairings; plus the model 'shape change at pattern places, repeating key elsewhere'
k4_result: Part A: clue pairs within one stroke: 7 of 24 (16-segment), 8 (5x7 dots, adds H->N), 7 (stroke list): E->F, O->Q, R->P twice, I->T, S->S, K->K. Corrected p (best of six statistics) 0.0016 against random pairing of the same letters (expected 1.9-2.5 near pairs); 0.0014 against any letter moved by the same alphabet distance; 0.011 against the same letters paired with the same alphabet-distance profile (expected 3.7-4.3); 0.21 with plain letter and alphabet distance kept and only the direction random (expected 5.0-6.0). The pre-set gate (corrected p < 0.01 under the profile-matched control) was NOT passed: 0.0112, four chains 0.010-0.012. Part B, run for the record: the near places 21, 26, 27, 32, 65, 67, 73 (0-based) form no pattern (best count 4-5, p 0.26-0.76 against random places; no period 2-13 splits them cleanly). Mask of residue classes mod 2-13 plus a repeating key of 1-12: 0 of 4,784 settings fit the clue letters. ANY set of near clue places masked plus a repeating key: 0 of 362,408. Every place a shape change: best readings score -6.14 / -6.89 / -7.66 on the big model, word coverage 0.28 / 0.16 / 0.16, not English, clue words absent.
controls: 200 shuffled K4s: near pairs median 3 / 2 / 1, at least K4's count in 3 / 0 / 0 of 200; 0 of 200 have a surviving setting in either exact test (but most have few near pairs, so only a median of 184 and 6,408 settings each). 200 texts with K4's own 24 clue pairs moved to random clue places and the rest shuffled (same near pairs, same number of settings as K4): 0 of 200 have a survivor in either test; pattern count at least K4's in 146 / 53 / 146 of 200. All-places-masked reading: 144 / 117 / 163 of 200 shuffles score at least as well as K4.
planted: 36/36: English texts with one-stroke changes at every 3rd, 4th or 5th place and a repeating key of 4-8 elsewhere (all three codings, both key numberings, four strip layouts, Vigenere and Beaufort). Each was found by both exact tests and read back with 0-4 wrong letters of 97; the true text was the top reading in 35 of 36. Part A saw 31 of 36 (near count above the 99% point of random pairing).
scope_limits: The three codings were written by the worker after the idea named the pairs, so every p is after the fact and too small; the stroke list is one person's choice of strokes. The 24 pairs are not independent draws (R->P counts twice). Half of the one-stroke pairs of the alphabet are also within 2 places of each other (E/F, O/Q, P/R), so shape and Bean closeness cannot be fully separated on 24 pairs; the four controls bracket it (0.0014 to 0.21). Part B covers only: masked places = residue classes mod 2-13 (or any subset of near clue places), unmasked places under ONE repeating key of length 1-12, Vigenere/Beaufort, A-Z or KRYPTOS strips, key numbered by position or by unmasked letters. Not covered: a non-repeating or long key at the unmasked places (then nothing can be tested), keyword-mixed alphabets other than KRYPTOS, shape rules of two or more strokes, lower-case or serif forms, Sanborn's real stencil shapes (not in the repository), transposition before or after.

negative.family: letter shapes (stroke added or cut away)
negative.hypothesis: At some pattern of places the K4 cipher letter is the plain letter with one stroke added or cut (E->F, R->P, O->Q, I->T), an ordinary key covers the rest, and the clue pairs are closer in shape than alphabet closeness explains.
negative.scope: Three fixed shape codings (16-segment <= 2 segments, 5x7 dot matrix <= 5 dots, block-capital stroke list <= 1 stroke); statistic on the 24 clue pairs against 100,000 pairings in each of four controls; model with masked places = residue classes mod 2-13 or any subset of the shape-near clue places, the rest under one repeating key of length 1-12 (Vigenere/Beaufort, A-Z and KRYPTOS strips, key numbered by position or by unmasked letters); 367,192 settings on K4.
negative.outcome: No signal: 7-8 of 24 clue pairs are within one stroke, corrected p 0.0016 against random pairing but 0.011 against pairings with the same alphabet-distance profile (pre-set gate 0.01 not passed) and 0.21 when plain letter and alphabet distance are kept; the hypothesis was made after seeing the pairs. Dead in the model's scope: the near places form no pattern (p 0.26-0.76) and 0 of 367,192 mask-plus-repeating-key settings fit the clue letters (controls: 0 of 200 shuffled K4s and 0 of 200 texts with K4's clue pairs moved; planted 36/36 found and read).

follow_ups: Get Sanborn's real letter forms: trace the 26 capitals from a straight-on photograph of the copper (data not in the repository) and redo part A with that single coding, fixed before any p is computed; one coding instead of three removes most of the after-the-fact freedom.

The same statistic on K1-K3 as a calibration: with their known plaintext, count cipher/plain pairs within one stroke against the same four controls. If K1-K3 (plain Quagmire III) also show an excess, the K4 excess is a by-product of the KRYPTOS tableau and alphabet order, not of shapes.
